chunks: From what was narrated by ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar, who said:

I asked Abā al-Ḥasan Mūsā عليه السلام about a house upon whose roof urine falls, and in which ghusl from janābah is performed; then water reaches it. May water be taken from its water and used for wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer)? He said: “If it flows, then there is no harm in it.”

key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the house or structure being asked about in the ruling
key_terms.الْجَنَابَةِ: the state of major ritual impurity requiring ghusl
key_terms.الْمَاءُ: water, the substance under legal discussion
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; expressing permissibility
key_terms.لِلصَّلَاةِ: for salat (prayer), showing the act of worship connected to the ruling
key_terms.يُبَالُ: urine is passed; indicating contact with impurity

ai.seo_question: Can water that reaches a place exposed to urine or janābah be used for wudu (ablution) if it is flowing?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning water that comes into contact with a place associated with impurity. Imam Mūsā عليه السلام states that if the water is flowing, there is no problem in using it for wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer), indicating the legal relevance of running water in rulings of taharah.
